sections.title: David as King over Judah
sections.description: David rules in Hebron over Judah while the civil war with the house of Saul continues

sections.title: David as King over All Israel
sections.description: Jerusalem is captured and becomes the capital, the ark of the covenant is brought in, God's covenant with David, and great military victories

sections.title: David's Sin and Its Consequences
sections.description: David's fall with Bathsheba and the serious consequences for his family and kingdom, including Absalom's rebellion

sections.title: Appendix
sections.description: David's last songs, the list of his mighty men, and the census with its consequences

events.title: David Learns of Saul's Death
events.description: An Amalekite comes to David in Ziklag with news that Saul and Jonathan have fallen in battle on Mount Gilboa. The man claims he killed Saul at his own request. David mourns deeply, tears his clothes, and fasts. He composes a moving lament over Saul and Jonathan, known as the 'Song of the Bow.'

events.title: David Anointed King over Judah
events.description: David asks the Lord and is told to go up to Hebron. There the men of Judah anoint him king over Judah. David sends word to the people of Jabesh Gilead and blesses them for burying Saul.

events.title: War between the House of David and the House of Saul
events.description: Abner, Saul's commander, makes Ish-Bosheth king over the rest of Israel. A long civil war breaks out. At the pool of Gibeon, twelve men from each side meet in a deadly duel, followed by a fierce battle where Abner kills David's nephew Asahel during the retreat.

events.title: Abner Defects to David and Is Killed by Joab
events.description: After a dispute over Saul's concubine Rizpah, Abner breaks with Ish-Bosheth and begins negotiating with David to unite all Israel under him. David demands that Michal, Saul's daughter, be returned to him. But Joab lures Abner back to Hebron and kills him to avenge his brother Asahel. David curses Joab and publicly mourns for Abner.

events.title: Ish-Bosheth Assassinated
events.description: Two of Ish-Bosheth's own commanders, Rechab and Baana, sneak in while he rests at midday and kill him. They bring his head to David in Hebron expecting a reward, but David is angry and has them executed for killing an innocent man in his own house.

events.title: David Anointed King over All Israel
events.description: All the tribes of Israel come to David at Hebron and acknowledge him as king. They make a covenant with him before the Lord, and David is anointed king over all Israel. At that time he had reigned seven and a half years over Judah in Hebron.

events.title: David Conquers Jerusalem
events.description: David and his men march against Jerusalem, which is held by the Jebusites. Despite the Jebusites' taunt that even the blind and lame could defend the city, David captures the fortress of Zion through the water shafts. Jerusalem becomes "the City of David" and the new capital of the united kingdom.

events.title: Victory over the Philistines
events.description: The Philistines march out twice against David after hearing that he has become king over all Israel. Both times David seeks the Lord's will. In the first battle, he defeats them at Baal-Perazim; in the second, he is told to circle around and attack from behind the balsam trees. Both times the Lord gives him victory.

events.title: The Ark of the Covenant Brought to Jerusalem
events.description: David gathers thirty thousand chosen men to bring the Ark of the Covenant from the house of Abinadab. The first attempt ends in tragedy when Uzzah reaches out his hand toward the ark and is struck dead by God. The ark is placed in the house of Obed-Edom for three months. On the second attempt, David follows the instructions, and the ark is carried into Jerusalem with rejoicing and the blowing of horns. David dances with all his might before the Lord, wearing a linen priestly garment.

events.title: God's Covenant with David
events.description: David wishes to build a temple for the Lord, but through the prophet Nathan God reveals that it is He who will build a house for David. God promises that David's descendant shall sit on the throne forever, and that his kingdom shall stand firm forever. This is one of the most important covenants in the Bible, with messianic promises pointing forward to Christ. David responds with a humble prayer of thanksgiving.

events.title: David's Military Victories
events.description: David leads a series of victorious wars. He subdues the Philistines, Moabites, Hadadezer king of Aram from Zobah, and the Edomites. He places garrisons in Aram and Edom. The Lord gives David victory wherever he goes. The kingdom expands greatly, and David rules with justice and righteousness.

events.title: David Shows Kindness to Mephibosheth
events.description: David seeks out survivors from Saul's house to show them kindness for Jonathan's sake. He finds Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, who is lame in both feet. David restores all of Saul's land to him and lets him eat at the king's table as one of his own sons.

events.title: The War Against the Ammonites
events.description: When the Ammonite king dies, David sends messengers to show sympathy. But the new king Hanun humiliates them by shaving off half their beards and cutting their garments in two. The Ammonites hire Aramean mercenaries, but Joab and Abishai defeat them in two battles. David himself goes out and defeats the Arameans at Helam.

events.title: David and Bathsheba
events.description: While Joab besieges Rabbah, David remains in Jerusalem. One evening he sees from the roof a beautiful woman bathing. It is Bathsheba, wife of the Hittite Uriah. David sends for her and lies with her, and she becomes pregnant. To hide his sin, David recalls Uriah from the front, but Uriah refuses to go home while the ark and the army are in the field. Finally, David sends him back with a letter to Joab ordering that Uriah be placed at the front of the battle and left there. Uriah falls in combat.

events.title: Nathan Confronts David
events.description: The prophet Nathan comes to David with a parable about a rich man who takes a poor man's only lamb. David becomes furious and sentences the rich man to death. Then Nathan says: "You are the man!" He proclaims God's judgment: the sword shall never depart from David's house, and disaster shall rise from his own family. David confesses his sin, and Nathan says that the Lord forgives him, but the child shall die.

events.title: The Child's Death and Solomon's Birth
events.description: The newborn child becomes ill. David fasts and prays for seven days, but the child dies. David rises, washes himself, worships God, and says: "Can I bring him back? I will go to him, but he will not return to me." Then David comforts Bathsheba, and she bears Solomon, whom the Lord loves.

events.title: Amnon and Tamar
events.description: David's firstborn son Amnon falls in love with his half-sister Tamar. He follows Jonadab's scheme, pretends to be sick, and asks Tamar to come and care for him. He rapes her, and afterward he hates her even more than he loved her. Absalom, Tamar's brother, says nothing but harbors deep hatred toward Amnon. David becomes furious but does nothing.

events.title: Absalom Kills Amnon
events.description: After two years, Absalom invites all the king's sons to sheep shearing in Baal-Hazor. He orders his servants to kill Amnon when he is drunk with wine. The other royal sons flee. Absalom flees to his maternal grandfather, the king of Geshur, and remains in exile for three years.

events.title: Absalom's Revolt
events.description: After returning to Jerusalem, Absalom wins the hearts of the Israelites by standing at the city gate and promising them justice. After four years, he launches his revolt from Hebron. David must flee Jerusalem with his loyal men. Hushai is sent back as a spy. Absalom follows Hushai's advice instead of Ahithophel's wise counsel, giving David time to organize his defense.

events.title: The Death of Absalom
events.description: The battle takes place in the forest of Ephraim. David divides his army into three and explicitly orders them to spare Absalom. While fleeing, Absalom's hair gets caught in a large terebinth tree while his mule runs on beneath him. Joab thrusts three spears through his heart despite David's command. When David receives the news, he breaks down in grief: "My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you!"

events.title: David Returns to Jerusalem
events.description: Joab rebukes David for his excessive grief, which is demoralizing the army. David rises and takes his place at the gate. The tribe of Judah invites him back, and he crosses the Jordan. Shimei, who cursed David during his flight, begs for mercy and receives it. Mephibosheth meets David and explains that Ziba deceived him. David divides the property between them.

events.title: Sheba's Revolt
events.description: The Benjamite Sheba blows a trumpet and shouts: "We have no share in David!" The northern tribes follow him in a new revolt. David appoints Amasa as commander, but Joab kills Amasa by stabbing him with his sword under the guise of greeting him. Joab pursues Sheba to Abel-Beth-Maacah, where a wise woman negotiates: the townspeople throw Sheba's head over the wall, and the revolt ends.

events.title: David's Song of Praise and Last Words
events.description: David sings a powerful song of praise to the Lord for deliverance from all his enemies, nearly identical to Psalm 18. This is followed by David's last words, in which he speaks of the righteous ruler and God's eternal covenant with his house.

events.title: The Census and the Plague
events.description: David orders a census of Israel and Judah despite Joab's warnings. After the count, conscience strikes David, and he confesses his sin. The prophet Gad gives him a choice among three punishments: three years of famine, three months of fleeing from enemies, or three days of plague. David chooses the plague and entrusts himself to God's mercy. Seventy thousand people die. The angel stretches out his hand toward Jerusalem, but the Lord relents and stops the plague at the threshing floor of the Jebusite Araunah. David buys the site and builds an altar, and the plague stops. This is where Solomon's temple will later be built.
